name: serial-fiction
description: Fiction released in installments over time (a web serial, a Substack/Patreon serial, an episodic series) rather than as a single complete work — each chapter is read both on its own and as part of an ongoing whole.

brief_fields.name: logline
brief_fields.label: Logline
brief_fields.prompt: What's the serial, in one or two sentences?

brief_fields.name: release_cadence
brief_fields.label: Release cadence
brief_fields.prompt: How often do new chapters/episodes go out — weekly, biweekly, irregular?

brief_fields.name: audience
brief_fields.label: Audience
brief_fields.prompt: Who's the target audience, and where do they read this (platform)?

brief_fields.name: comps
brief_fields.label: Comps
brief_fields.prompt: A couple of comparable serials or published books it sits beside?

brief_fields.name: hook_expectation
brief_fields.label: Hook expectation
brief_fields.prompt: How strict should the "ends on a hook or compelling beat" convention be — every chapter, most chapters, or only when it fits naturally? Chapters not fully resolving is expected craft here, not a defect.

draft_stages.name: exploratory / partial
draft_stages.implication: Structure only. No line-level findings at all — the prose isn't real yet.

draft_stages.name: first complete draft
draft_stages.implication: Developmental focus. Line findings only if major+ or a manuscript-wide pattern.

draft_stages.name: revised
draft_stages.implication: Both layers in full, normal severity calibration.

draft_stages.name: ready to post
draft_stages.implication: Both layers, and minor findings become worth reporting — this is the version that goes live.
